competency_fulfillment.rationale: All 6 samples use the identical stem 'A figure is made of a rectangle with a triangle on top. How many shapes make up this figure?', which only exercises decomposition-by-counting of a fixed 2-shape figure; 'compose' is never tested and circles, half circles, or quarter circles named in the competency never appear.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The question_text is byte-for-byte identical across all 6 seeds (42, 43, 44, 45, 46, 50); only which answer key (A-D) holds the value '2' changes, so no other composite figure, shape combination, or shape count is ever generated.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The single repeated sentence is simple enough for Grade 2, but its total invariance across all 6 seeds means the item never shows whether students can reason about figures with more than two parts or with curved pieces.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: There is no cut-outs framing, no square-grid framing, and no composition task anywhere in the 6 samples; every seed is the same 'rectangle with a triangle on top' decomposition-counting question in mcq or read_mcq dress.

competency_alignment.rationale: The only variation across seeds 42-50 is which answer key (A-D) holds the correct value '2', which tests MCQ-option scanning rather than composing or decomposing figures made of squares, rectangles, triangles, circles, half circles, or quarter circles.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The figure always has exactly 2 component shapes (one rectangle, one triangle) across all 6 seeds; the competency's implied range of composite complexity involving up to six named shape types is never scaled up.
